title: Model Card
description: The internal model card the team produces for every AI feature shipped to customers. Eight short sections — far lighter than the academic model-card papers, sized for an internal team that has 30 minutes to read it. The discipline is being honest in sections 5 (limitations) and 6 (known failure modes): if you skip those, the document is marketing not engineering.

# Model Card: [Feature name]
_v[N] · last updated [date] · owner [AIE]_

## 1. What this feature does (one paragraph)
_The capability, in plain English. The user-facing thing._

## 2. Models in use
_Generation model + version. Embedding model + version. Any retrieval / reranker models. Last reviewed for upgrade [date]._

## 3. Inputs / outputs
_What the feature accepts as input (length, language, content type). What it produces (format, length, structure)._

## 4. Training / evaluation data
_Where the eval golden set comes from. Where any few-shot examples come from. Where the RAG corpus comes from (if applicable). Any data we explicitly do NOT use._

## 5. Limitations
_The honest limits. Languages, topics, edge cases the system isn't good at. The team and stakeholders need to know this; it's the section users skip and then regret skipping when CS lands the question this section would have answered._

## 6. Known failure modes
_The specific ways this can go wrong, with frequency estimates if known. The Friday-hallucination kind of detail._

## 7. Performance + monitoring
_Headline eval score on the golden set. What we monitor in production. What triggers a paging alert._

## 8. Change history (link)
_Link to the prompt versioning changelog + any model upgrades. Not the full history embedded in this doc; just a pointer._

worked_examples.content_md:
# Model Card: Customer-KB Assistant
_v0.3 · last updated 22 May 2026 · owner [AIE]_

## 1. What this feature does

The Customer-KB Assistant lets internal CS team members ask natural-language questions of our customer-knowledge-base (3,200 markdown docs, updated weekly) and receive cited responses. Used for ~40 daily active CS users for ticket-context retrieval, account-policy lookup, and cross-product question answering.

## 2. Models in use

- **Generation:** Claude Sonnet 4.5 (anthropic.com)
- **Embedding:** OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072 dim)
- **Retrieval/rerank:** none (heuristic ranking only; cross-encoder reranker on the v2 roadmap)
- Last reviewed for model upgrade: 18 April 2026 (ADR-014).

## 3. Inputs / outputs

- **Input:** free-text question. Max 500 characters in v1 (truncated with a UI message above that). English only at v1.
- **Output:** ~200-500 token response in plain English, with citations by document H1/H2 path. Always cites at least one source, or says 'not found in the knowledge base' explicitly.
- **Latency:** P95 <3s. Pages on >5s.

## 4. Training / evaluation data

- **Golden set:** 184 hand-curated question-answer pairs, sampled from real CS tickets (anonymised), versioned in `evals/customer-kb-assistant/golden-set.jsonl`. Originally seeded from 60 example tickets in week 4; expanded over time.
- **RAG corpus:** the customer-knowledge-base markdown repo. Weekly snapshot, embeddings rebuilt on snapshot.
- **Explicitly NOT used:** customer-specific data, ticket content, internal financial documents, employee handbooks.

## 5. Limitations

- **English only at v1.** ~12% of internal users are native non-English speakers; the system works in their case but is not validated for non-English query patterns.
- **No multi-turn memory in v1.** Each query is independent; the system does not remember prior turns. Users sometimes assume otherwise.
- **Recency.** The corpus updates weekly; a policy change made on Monday won't be retrievable until the next weekly snapshot (Friday).
- **Coverage.** The corpus does not include sales-confidential pricing or HR handbooks; the system will say 'not found' for those topics rather than refuse, which can be confusing.

## 6. Known failure modes

- **Policy invention (rare, ~0.3% in beta):** the system occasionally invents a policy that doesn't exist when asked leading questions. The 14 May incident was an example. Mitigated in prompt v3 + the refund-policy eval; we believe the residual rate is <0.1% but cannot confirm without more production data.
- **Citation drift (~2% in beta):** the system cites the right document but the wrong paragraph in it. Working hypothesis: chunking-boundary issues. Documented; will likely be fixed when the cross-encoder reranker is added.
- **Over-cautious responses on legitimate questions (~5% in beta):** when the question is borderline (e.g. 'what should I do if a customer asks me X'), the system sometimes refuses to engage even when a clear KB answer exists. Tuning underway.

## 7. Performance + monitoring

- **Current eval score:** 31/32 on critical refund-policy subset; 152/184 (83%) on full set.
- **Production monitoring:** P95 latency, error rate, eval-replay-on-production-conversations weekly.
- **Paging triggers:** P95 >5s for 5 min; error rate >2%; nightly eval replay drops below 80% on full set.

## 8. Change history

- Prompt changelog: `prompts/customer-kb-assistant/changelog.md`
- Architecture decisions: ADR-014 (initial RAG architecture), ADR-019 (May refund-policy prompt update post-incident).

annotations.note: One paragraph. The team member who's never used the feature should understand what it does after reading just this. The user-facing capability — not the architecture.
Models named with versions. 'Claude' is not enough; 'Claude Sonnet 4.5' is. The 'last reviewed for upgrade' date is the trigger for the next model-comparison conversation.

Limitations honestly named. The 'English only' note isn't a feature gap, it's a usage-pattern caveat. Same for 'no multi-turn'. These are the limitations CS will run into and need to know about before they hit them.

Known failure modes with quantified frequency. The 0.3% policy-invention rate is the kind of honest detail that builds trust with the eng lead and the manager — versus 'rare but possible' which is the unfalsifiable rookie phrase.

Paging triggers explicit. The on-call AIE wakes up only for specific thresholds, not 'something feels off'. Clear thresholds prevent the team from getting woken up for noise + ensure real incidents get attention.

common_mistakes: Limitations section omitted because 'we don't want to undersell the feature'. Wrong audience — model cards are internal, not marketing. Be honest.
Known-failure-modes section omitted. Stakeholders find them in production instead of in the doc, and the doc loses credibility.
Model version not specified. 'Claude' is not a model. 'Claude Sonnet 4.5' is.
Eval scores quoted without saying 'on what'. '95% accurate' is meaningless without the golden set named.
Paging triggers vague ('on errors'). The team gets paged for noise and stops trusting alerts.
Change history embedded inline rather than linked. Model cards get long; link to the changelogs and ADRs.
variant_patterns: Customer-facing model card variant: heavier on limitations, lighter on internal architecture. Designed to be read by customers / auditors / compliance.

Multi-model card variant: a system using two models for different layers (e.g. a small model for routing + a larger one for generation) gets one model card per model, plus an orchestration card describing how they compose.
Pre-launch model card variant: §5-7 written in expectations rather than measurements. Marked 'pre-launch' clearly; reviewed at week 4 of production with measurements.
